diagnose_rules.text: A campaign that spent nothing and showed nothing was never in the auction: bids below the page floor, disapproved ads, a budget of zero, or a wrong geography. Fix the setup, do not judge the channel.
Broad match on short terms buys the platform's guesses. Cheap clicks with near-zero conversion on terms that only share a word with the offer point at match type, not demand.
When the ad account only counts an upstream event such as a scan or a form view, the reported cost per conversion says nothing about customers. Import the purchase before judging.
Click-through above 1.5% with cost per acquisition above 1.5 times target means the ad works and the page does not. Audit message match, load time, mobile and the single call to action.
Several campaigns sharing a small budget starve each other before any reaches a read. One campaign, one goal, until it has thirty conversions.
Conversions that all arrive from the business's own name prove nothing about buying new demand; brand defence is a separate decision.
When the realised cost per click already exceeds what the allowable acquisition cost can carry at any plausible conversion rate, the auction is too expensive for the price point.
Conversions recorded without a click identifier or transaction id cannot be trusted either way; enhanced conversions or server-side import come before the next dollar.
